settings.heading: How to Take
settings.body: Fill the dropper to the line and release it under your tongue. Hold it there for 60 seconds, then swallow. Once a day, ideally with your morning routine. One bottle is 30 servings.

settings.heading: Why Under the Tongue?
settings.body: The pigments in MacuDrops are micellized in MCT oil and sunflower lecithin, so they’re already dispersed when they reach the thin tissue under your tongue. A capsule has to break down in your stomach first, and fat-soluble carotenoids like lutein are known to absorb poorly that way.

settings.heading: Taking Other Treatments?
settings.body: MacuDrops is a dietary supplement. It does not replace injections, laser or any treatment your eye doctor prescribes. Keep every appointment. Show your ophthalmologist the ingredient list, especially if you take blood thinners, because ginkgo biloba can affect bleeding.

settings.q: How long until I notice anything?
settings.a: Macular pigment builds gradually. Research on lutein and zeaxanthin usually measures changes over 3 to 6 months of daily use, so we recommend giving MacuDrops at least 3 months.*

settings.q: Does MacuDrops replace my eye injections or laser treatment?
settings.a: No. MacuDrops is a dietary supplement, not a treatment for any eye disease. If you have diabetic retinopathy, macular degeneration or any other eye condition, keep every appointment and follow your eye doctor’s treatment plan.

settings.q: Is it safe with my medications?
settings.a: Show the ingredient list to your doctor before starting, especially if you take blood thinners (warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel), because ginkgo biloba can affect bleeding. Ask your doctor if you are pregnant or nursing.
